problem.passage:
Text 1

Coral reefs occupy less than one percent of the ocean floor yet support roughly a quarter of all marine species. Some marine biologists argue that reef restoration efforts should prioritize "super corals"—genetically selected strains that survive unusually warm or acidic water. By outplanting these resilient strains across degraded reefs, researchers hope to create a scaffold of living coral that can persist even as ocean temperatures continue to rise. Critics of conventional restoration note that simply replanting whatever coral is locally available often fails, since the same conditions that killed the original reef will likely kill the replacements within a few years, wasting scarce conservation funding.

Text 2

While selectively bred "super corals" survive laboratory stress tests, their long-term performance in the wild remains unproven, and some reef ecologists worry that a restoration strategy centered on a narrow set of resilient genotypes could inadvertently reduce the genetic diversity of a reef system. A reef built from a handful of hardy strains may resist heat spikes better in the short term, but it could also become more vulnerable to disease outbreaks or unexpected environmental shifts that the original, more diverse population would have withstood. These researchers advocate instead for preserving a broad genetic pool, even if that means accepting some short-term losses.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the proposal, described in Text 1, that restoration should prioritize outplanting super corals across degraded reefs?

problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the proposal, described in Text 1, that restoration should prioritize outplanting super corals across degraded reefs?
options: The author would endorse the proposal, since super corals have already demonstrated superior long-term survival in wild reef systems compared with genetically diverse populations.

The author would agree that heat-resistant strains offer short-term protection but would caution that relying mainly on them could leave reefs with less genetic diversity and thus more exposed to threats like disease.

The author would reject the proposal outright, insisting that any reliance on a narrow set of resilient strains is just as likely to fail as the conventional replanting approach that Text 1's critics describe.

The author would maintain that Text 1's critics of conventional restoration are right to worry about wasted funding, but would insist that this risk applies equally to super corals, since their genetic narrowness could itself cause restoration failures within a few years.
problem.explanation: Text 2는 super coral이 단기적으로 내열성을 보인다는 점은 인정하지만(“A reef built from a handful of hardy strains may resist heat spikes better in the short term”), 그런 좁은 유전자 풀에 의존하면 장기적으로는 질병 등 다른 위협에 더 취약해질 수 있다고 한정한다(“it could also become more vulnerable to disease outbreaks or unexpected environmental shifts that the original, more diverse population would have withstood”). 따라서 Text 2의 저자는 Text 1의 super coral 중심 제안에 대해 단기적 이점은 인정하되 장기적 위험을 경고하는 방식으로 반응할 것이다.
problem.evidenceTarget: Text 2는 Text 1이 제안한 super coral 중심 복원 전략이 단기적으로는 내열성을 높이지만 장기적으로는 유전적 다양성을 줄여 질병 등 다른 위협에 취약해질 수 있다고 한정한다.
problem.evidenceSpan: A reef built from a handful of hardy strains may resist heat spikes better in the short term, but it could also become more vulnerable to disease outbreaks or unexpected environmental shifts that the original, more diverse population would have withstood.
problem.answerRationale: Text 2가 super coral의 단기 내열성은 인정(“resist heat spikes better in the short term”)하면서도 좁은 유전자 풀이 질병 등에 대한 장기적 취약성을 낳을 수 있다고 경고(“more vulnerable to disease outbreaks... that the original, more diverse population would have withstood”)하므로, 두 텍스트를 종합하면 저자는 Text 1의 제안에 대해 조건부 동의와 경고를 함께 표할 것이라는 결론이 도출된다.

difficultyReasons: 두 지문(Text1, Text2)의 관계를 종합해 Text2 저자의 입장을 추론해야 함(2단계 이상)
정답은 '단기적 인정+장기적 우려'라는 미묘한 균형을 정확히 짚어야 함
오답 A는 명백한 반대 진술로 쉽게 제거 가능하나, C와 D는 정답과 유사한 부정적 뉴앙스를 공유해 변별이 필요함
특히 D는 Text1의 표현을 재사용해 그럴듯하게 만들어 신중한 대조가 필요함

distractors.plausibleBecause: Text 2가 super corals의 실험실 생존력을 인정하는 문장이 있어 '지지'로 오해할 수 있다
distractors.matches: 'selectively bred super corals survive laboratory stress tests'라는 부분
distractors.whyWrong: Text 2는 야생에서의 장기 성능이 '증명되지 않았다(unproven)'고 명시하며, 유전 다양성 감소 우려로 신중한 입장을 취하므로 '이미 우월성이 입증됐다'는 주장은 지문과 정반대다

distractors.plausibleBecause: Text 2가 super corals 전략에 우려를 표하므로 완전히 거부한다고 확대 해석할 수 있다
distractors.matches: 'could inadvertently reduce genetic diversity', 'more vulnerable to disease' 등 부정적 뉴앙스
distractors.whyWrong: Text 2는 super corals이 '단기적으로는 열 스트레스에 더 잘 견딘다'는 점을 인정하며, '실패할 것'이라 단정하지 않고 장기적 위험(질병, 예상치 못한 환경 변화)에 대한 우려를 제기하는 균형잡힌 입장이므로 '거부'는 과장이다

distractors.plausibleBecause: Text 1의 비판자들이 언급한 '자금 낭비' 문제를 super corals에도 적용시켜 일관성 있어 보이게 만든 선택지
distractors.matches: 'wasting scarce conservation funding'과 'within a few years'라는 Text 1의 표현을 그대로 차용
distractors.whyWrong: Text 2는 자금 낭비나 몇 년 내 실패라는 구체적 시간 프레임을 언급하지 않으며, 오히려 질병 발생이나 예측 불가능한 환경 변화 같은 장기적·다른 종류의 위험을 우려하는 것이므로 Text 1의 논리를 그대로 복사한 것은 왜곡이다
